synopsis: ISO 34503:2023 specifies how to describe an operational design domain (ODD), using a hierarchical structure; domain definition sets testing boundaries and therefore determines what coverage means [f15315, f6706, f6782]. Its normative scope is automated road vehicles, with lanes and junctions dominating default attributes, so the booklet transfers its architecture and process to off-road validation rather than treating its content as off-road compliance evidence [f6709, f7182, f15320]. The booklet uses ISO 3450x layering and ODD taxonomy to organize off-road scenarios, but warns that off-road taxonomies remain immature; its proposed taxonomy combines ISO 34503/OpenODD with ODD-UM and EMESRT and is explicitly expert opinion [f15327, f6714]. A November 2025 agricultural ODD proposal also borrows ISO 34503 concepts, providing another example of adaptation rather than demonstrated off-road validity [f1399, f7696]. For planning, the scenario standards require coverage to reflect the ODD but focus on coverage rather than model credibility: they do not address validation against physical data or risk scaling, and establish no physical-to-virtual testing ratio [f8121, f8120, f8119, f7694].
